title: LLAMA LIMA: A Living Meta-Analysis on the Effects of Generative AI on Learning Mathematics (Version 3, 05/26)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the rapidly changing evidence base on whether generative AI tools improve mathematics learning. Because generative AI technologies and related studies are evolving quickly, the authors argue that conventional static reviews risk becoming outdated. They therefore present LLAMA LIMA, a versioned living meta-analysis designed to be repeatedly updated as new experimental and quasi-experimental evidence becomes available.

The approach is a living systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA-LSR guidance. For Version 3, the authors searched SCOPUS and SCOPUS Preprints through April 1, 2026, and included studies that used generative AI in a mathematics-learning intervention with a non-generative-AI control group and mathematics performance outcomes. The analysis included 24 studies, 58 effect sizes, and 3,800 participants. Effects were synthesized with a Bayesian multilevel meta-regression model, and moderators included educational level, mathematical content, AI purpose, intervention characteristics, integration mode, assessment type, publication type, and research setting.

The included evidence spans multiple learner levels, including primary/lower secondary, secondary, post-secondary/tertiary, and adult learners, across varied mathematics education contexts. The paper does not report a single country, setting, or intervention duration because it aggregates multiple primary studies. Some interventions used generative AI as a mathematics expert, tutor, instructor, or teacher-support tool.

The pooled effect of generative AI interventions on mathematics learning was positive but uncertain, with Hedges’ g = 0.40 and a 95% credible interval of [0.14, 0.67]. Moderator analyses found moderate evidence that generative AI was more beneficial when it supplemented regular instruction than when it replaced teachers. Evidence for most other moderators remained limited. The authors conclude that generative AI may support mathematics learning, especially when integrated with teacher-led instruction, but the evidence base is still small, heterogeneous, and in need of continued updating.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI systems, including large-language-model-based tools and custom AI supports, used to generate mathematical explanations, feedback, solutions, tutoring support, instructional materials, or related learning assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper synthesized experimental and quasi-experimental studies comparing mathematics learning interventions that used generative AI with control conditions that did not use generative AI.

findings.finding_summary: Across 24 studies, 58 effect sizes, and exactly n=3,800 participants, generative AI–based instructional interventions had a positive pooled effect on mathematics learning outcomes (Hedges’ g=0.40, 95% CrI [0.14, 0.67]). Publication-bias assessment found weak evidence against publication bias (BF=0.29; posterior probability=.22), with a model-averaged median effect of g=0.33, 95% CrI [0.00, 0.61]. Moderator analyses found moderate evidence that supplementing regular instruction produced larger effects (g=0.65) than replacing teachers (g=0.16), BF10=8.72.
findings.measure: Mathematics learning outcomes / mathematics performance, analyzed as standardized mean differences using Hedges’ g

quality_tier_rationale: This is a quantitative living meta-analysis following PRISMA-LSR procedures, synthesizing 24 experimental or quasi-experimental studies with 58 effect sizes and n=3,800 participants. The paper is a preprint and notes limited evidence and heterogeneity, but the design is still a formal meta-analysis.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled effect of generative AI–based mathematics interventions was medium and positive (Hedges’ g=0.40, 95% CrI [0.14, 0.67]), exceeding the ≥0.20 threshold. A publication-bias-adjusted model also remained positive (g=0.33, 95% CrI [0.00, 0.61]).
